bull_bear.body: 100% focused on capex for smart knitting machines; No dividends or buybacks mentioned; No new debt raised; Supplier financing eliminates need for external capital; Working capital managed efficiently (positive OCF)
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: US tariff uncertainty impacting demand visibility; Slow adoption in new European markets; Competitive pressure from displaced Chinese/other Indian suppliers; Execution risk in 3-year machine rollout; Labor cost inflation if wage hikes persist beyond 2026
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and strategic — framing US trade disruption as temporary, emphasizing automation as non-negotiable future, highlighting supplier financing as a strength, projecting Rs.700Cr revenue target with clear roadmap; tone is optimistic but grounded in operational discipline
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The Rs.60Cr capex is not a cash outflow — it’s supplier-financed machinery; the real capital risk is borne by Ningbo, not Active Clothing; this is a rare case of capex being funded by equipment vendor — a structural advantage
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated design-to-manufacturing capability, described as an important competitive advantage, letting the Company support customers seeking flexibility, product differentiation and shorter development cycles
- Ability to engage brands across the full chain from product conception and development through manufacturing, distribution and retail
- Long-standing relationships with established domestic and international brands
- Manufacturing flexibility and design capabilities positioned as a platform for continued product development
- Captive renewable generation: an installed solar system of approximately 503.04 kWp DC / 500 kW AC reducing dependence on conventional electricity
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw-material price volatility — Profitability can be affected by fluctuations in the prices of yarn, fabrics and other raw materials; the Company says it manages this through procurement planning, customer relationships, product pricing and operational efficiencies. Pricing pressure in the industry already showed up as a moderation in the EBITDA margin during FY26.
- Customer concentration — The Company states that dependence on large customers can create concentration risk, and that it continues to work towards expanding its customer base, product portfolio and business channels. Its historical model of serving a set of established brands makes the loss or order reduction of a single brand structurally material.
- Demand and fashion risk — Apparel demand is influenced by changing consumer preferences, fashion cycles, weather conditions and broader economic trends - a particular exposure given the Company's weighting towards winter wear and knitted apparel. Mitigation claimed is product diversification, customer diversification and quick response to changing product requirements.
- Execution risk on new businesses, notably the NUEMO retail platform — The Company says the success of new initiatives, particularly the NUEMO retail platform, depends on effective execution, store economics, customer acceptance, supply-chain management and prudent capital deployment, and separately acknowledges that expansion into organised multi-brand retail involves execution, capital-allocation and market-acceptance risks. This takes the Company outside its B2B manufacturing competence.
- Working-capital intensity — Manufacturing and distribution require working capital for inventory, receivables and operating expenses; the Company names efficient inventory management, receivable collection and prudent financial management as important priorities, and cites working-capital strengthening as a use of the proposed fundraising.
- Foreign exchange and global-market exposure — Exposure to international customers and global supply chains may subject the Company to foreign-exchange movements and geopolitical or macroeconomic developments; the Company says it monitors such developments and acts within its operating framework. The MD&A separately cites tariff actions, conflict-driven freight and energy costs, and sourcing realignments as live disruptions.
- Competitive intensity in apparel manufacturing — The industry is described as highly competitive both domestically and internationally; the Company seeks to differentiate on quality, design capability, manufacturing flexibility, technology, customer service and integrated solutions, but pricing pressure and competitive intensity are named among the challenges that can affect operating performance.
- Regulatory and sustainability-compliance complexity — Management flags rapidly evolving requirements on product traceability, Extended Producer Responsibility, environmental disclosures and product compliance across jurisdictions, with the absence of harmonised global standards raising compliance costs and operational complexity for suppliers to international brands.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Sweaters: largest segment; Jackets & woven: growing; T-shirts & uppers: moderate; Export revenue: crossing Rs.100Cr in FY26; Domestic: ~75% of revenue; No new product categories — expansion within existing lines

business.body: The Company designs, develops and manufactures knitted apparel for established domestic and international brands, working with them from product conception and development through manufacturing, distribution and retail. Manufacturing capabilities cover flat-knit sweaters, jackets and circular-knit products, with additional capabilities in shoe uppers and other emerging categories. It has progressively broadened its portfolio into knitted accessories, soft-knitted toys and athleisure to reduce dependence on individual product categories.

outlook.body: Revenue growth: targeting Rs.700Cr total revenue post-600-machine rollout; Margin: expected to improve post-2027 automation efficiency gains; Order inflow: new audits underway with Primark, Marks & Spencer; Capex/commissioning: Rs.60Cr in FY26-27; full 600-machine rollout over 3 years (2027 end)
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.15Cr from Levi’s San Francisco division; additional sampling approved for Agilitas; Primark and M&S audits in progress (expected onboarding in 3-4 months)
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into European markets (UK, Germany); Potential entry into mass-market brands (Primark, M&S); Leveraging 3D design tech to attract new global clients; Long-term revenue upside to Rs.700Cr post-capex completion
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Maintain and deepen relationships with established domestic and international apparel brands while developing additional channels to diversify the revenue base
- Continue product diversification beyond core knitwear to reduce dependence on individual product categories
- Raise growth capital through a preferential issue of convertible warrants to fund future expansion, working capital and operational capabilities
- Reinvest earnings rather than distribute them: no dividend recommended for FY2025-26 in view of continuous expansion activities, with profit transferred to reserves
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company operates an integrated manufacturing facility in Punjab with capabilities across sweaters, jackets, T-shirts and other knitted products; the report says only that earlier Company disclosures had indicated significant installed capacities across these categories, and does not restate them. No new plant, line or capacity-addition project with a commissioning or ramp timeline is disclosed in this bundle. Expansion is instead framed around product diversification into knitted accessories, toys and athleisure, and around funding: during FY26 the Company initiated a preferential issue of up to 20 lakh convertible warrants at ₹115 per warrant, aggregating up to ₹23 crore, intended to support future expansion plans, strengthen working capital and enhance operational capabilities - described as aligned with a broader strategy of creating additional capacity for growth while maintaining financial flexibility, with implementation dependent on market conditions, execution capability and efficient deployment of capital. Directors state no dividend is recommended in view of continuous expansion activities. On the energy side the Company has installed a solar power system of approximately 503.04 kWp DC / 500 kW AC; this is captive generation, not manufacturing capacity. Management also lists expansion of the retail and distribution platform and entry into organised multi-brand retail (the NUEMO platform) as opportunities it intends to pursue, while acknowledging these carry execution, capital-allocation and market-acceptance risk - these remain stated intentions, not commissioned projects.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management cites reshaping of global sourcing patterns by US tariff actions, the Russia-Ukraine conflict and West Asia tensions as reinforcing the need for agile, geographically diversified and digitally-enabled sourcing platforms
- Political instability and labour disruptions in Bangladesh, described as one of the world's largest apparel manufacturing hubs, are cited as highlighting the importance of diversified sourcing networks - a stated shift in global sourcing preferences
- The MD&A states the global fashion industry is expected to deliver low single-digit growth in 2026 amid continued macroeconomic uncertainty, with consumers increasingly value conscious and more selective in discretionary spending
- Union Budget 2026-27 textile policy support is cited as a demand enabler: PM MITRA, the PLI Scheme for Textiles, and a new programme covering the National Fibre Scheme, the Textile Expansion and Employment (TEEM) Scheme, the Tex-Eco Initiative and Samarth 2.0, intended to position India as a competitive sourcing destination as brands diversify supply chains
- Listed apparel-market trends management points to: geographic shift in demand, digitalisation of the apparel value chain, changing consumer behaviour, sustainability becoming mainstream, and expansion of omnichannel retailing
- Flagged industry headwinds: trade-policy and tariff uncertainty raising sourcing costs, supply-chain and inventory volatility reducing order visibility, workforce transformation in the AI era, and rising sustainability-compliance and traceability requirements (including EPR)
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Active Clothing is scaling India's first knit-to-shape smart factory with 600 new machines to future-proof against US trade volatility, but near-term margins are pressured by temporary labor cost inflation and market uncertainty; the real catalyst is the 2027 commissioning of this facility, which could unlock Rs.700Cr revenue potential.

open.item: The Company initiated a preferential issue of up to 20 lakh convertible warrants at ₹115 per warrant, aggregating up to ₹23 crore, to fund future expansion plans, working capital and operational capabilities.

Management intends to keep diversifying beyond established sweater, jacket and circular-knit categories into knitted accessories, toys and athleisure to cut dependence on individual product categories and cross-sell to existing customers.

Management is pursuing the NUEMO retail platform as a new initiative in organised multi-brand retail, whose success it says will depend on execution, store economics, customer acceptance, supply-chain management and prudent capital deployment.
Management flags dependence on large customers as a concentration risk and says it continues to work towards expanding its customer base, product portfolio and business channels.
The Company's installed solar system of approximately 503.04 kWp DC / 500 kW AC has an expected first-year generation of approximately 655.48 MWh, according to the Company's solar-power disclosure.
Management flags that the global fashion industry is expected to deliver only low single-digit growth in 2026 amid continued macroeconomic uncertainty and increasingly value-conscious consumers.

Management flags that frequent changes in global trade policies and tariff regimes, rising import duties and country-of-origin scrutiny continue to add to sourcing costs and operational complexity across apparel supply chains.
Management flags that geopolitical disruptions, logistics challenges and tighter retailer inventory management continue to reduce order visibility and complicate production planning.

Management flags rising product-traceability, Extended Producer Responsibility, environmental-disclosure and product-compliance requirements across jurisdictions, with the absence of harmonised global standards raising compliance costs.

Management states the fundraising is aligned with a broader strategy of creating additional capacity for growth while maintaining financial flexibility, with success dependent on market conditions, execution capabilities and efficient deployment of capital.

Management lists expansion of the Company's retail and distribution platform and expansion into new product categories among the opportunities it intends to pursue, leveraging manufacturing capability, customer relationships and its technology platform.
The installed solar system is expected to generate approximately 655.48 MWh in its first year, per the Company's solar-power disclosure, reducing dependence on conventional electricity.

Manufacturing and distribution require working capital for inventory, receivables and operating expenses; the Company names efficient inventory management, receivable collection and prudent financial management as important priorities, and cites working-capital strengthening as a use of the proposed fundraising.

Exposure to international customers and global supply chains may subject the Company to foreign-exchange movements and geopolitical or macroeconomic developments; the Company says it monitors such developments and acts within its operating framework. The MD&A separately cites tariff actions, conflict-driven freight and energy costs, and sourcing realignments as live disruptions.

The industry is described as highly competitive both domestically and internationally; the Company seeks to differentiate on quality, design capability, manufacturing flexibility, technology, customer service and integrated solutions, but pricing pressure and competitive intensity are named among the challenges that can affect operating performance.

Management flags rapidly evolving requirements on product traceability, Extended Producer Responsibility, environmental disclosures and product compliance across jurisdictions, with the absence of harmonised global standards raising compliance costs and operational complexity for suppliers to international brands.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Active Clothing Co Limited is an integrated apparel company spanning design, product development, sourcing, manufacturing, distribution and retail, built around serving established domestic and international apparel brands.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company designs, develops and manufactures knitted apparel for established domestic and international brands, working with them from product conception and development through manufacturing, distribution and retail. Manufacturing capabilities cover flat-knit sweaters, jackets and circular-knit products, with additional capabilities in shoe uppers and other emerging categories. It has progressively broadened its portfolio into knitted accessories, soft-knitted toys and athleisure to reduce dependence on individual product categories.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Mrs. Renu Mehra — related party: Non-Executive Director and wife of the Managing Director Mr. Rajesh Kumar Mehra; professional fee paid to her, stated by the Company to be in the ordinary course of business and at arm's length, and not a material transaction under Regulation 23(1) of LODR
- Mrs. Kalika Mehra — related party: Daughter of directors Mr. Rajesh Kumar Mehra and Mrs. Renu Mehra; fee paid for professional services rendered, approved by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee and by special resolution of shareholders at the 20th AGM
- Guram Neutra Pharma P Limited — related party: Other company in which the Managing Director Mr. Rajesh Kumar Mehra is a Director, per the directorships table as on 31 March 2026; no shareholding or group relationship with Active Clothing Co Limited is stated

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Sweaters: largest segment; Jackets & woven: growing; T-shirts & uppers: moderate; Export revenue: crossing Rs.100Cr in FY26; Domestic: ~75% of revenue; No new product categories — expansion within existing lines

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Knitted apparel:** Flat-knit sweaters, Jackets, Circular-knit products, T-shirts
- **Knitted accessories:** Knitted beanies, Gloves
- **Emerging categories:** Shoe uppers, Soft-knitted toys, Athleisure products

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Established domestic apparel brands
- International apparel brands
- High-fashion winter wear and knitted apparel
- Organised retail in Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets
- Organised multi-brand retail via the NUEMO retail platform

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Rs.15Cr from Levi’s San Francisco division; additional sampling approved for Agilitas; Primark and M&S audits in progress (expected onboarding in 3-4 months)

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth: targeting Rs.700Cr total revenue post-600-machine rollout; Margin: expected to improve post-2027 automation efficiency gains; Order inflow: new audits underway with Primark, Marks & Spencer; Capex/commissioning: Rs.60Cr in FY26-27; full 600-machine rollout over 3 years (2027 end)

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into European markets (UK, Germany); Potential entry into mass-market brands (Primark, M&S); Leveraging 3D design tech to attract new global clients; Long-term revenue upside to Rs.700Cr post-capex completion

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management cites reshaping of global sourcing patterns by US tariff actions, the Russia-Ukraine conflict and West Asia tensions as reinforcing the need for agile, geographically diversified and digitally-enabled sourcing platforms
- Political instability and labour disruptions in Bangladesh, described as one of the world's largest apparel manufacturing hubs, are cited as highlighting the importance of diversified sourcing networks - a stated shift in global sourcing preferences
- The MD&A states the global fashion industry is expected to deliver low single-digit growth in 2026 amid continued macroeconomic uncertainty, with consumers increasingly value conscious and more selective in discretionary spending
- Union Budget 2026-27 textile policy support is cited as a demand enabler: PM MITRA, the PLI Scheme for Textiles, and a new programme covering the National Fibre Scheme, the Textile Expansion and Employment (TEEM) Scheme, the Tex-Eco Initiative and Samarth 2.0, intended to position India as a competitive sourcing destination as brands diversify supply chains
- Listed apparel-market trends management points to: geographic shift in demand, digitalisation of the apparel value chain, changing consumer behaviour, sustainability becoming mainstream, and expansion of omnichannel retailing
- Flagged industry headwinds: trade-policy and tariff uncertainty raising sourcing costs, supply-chain and inventory volatility reducing order visibility, workforce transformation in the AI era, and rising sustainability-compliance and traceability requirements (including EPR)

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q2 EBITDA margin dipped to 8.88% due to 8% YoY employee benefit cost increase (wages + benefits) — temporary labor inflation from retention needs amid market uncertainty; Raw material (cotton/yarn) stable; Margin recovery expected post-automation efficiency gains (labor + waste reduction) from 2027

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: 100% focused on capex for smart knitting machines; No dividends or buybacks mentioned; No new debt raised; Supplier financing eliminates need for external capital; Working capital managed efficiently (positive OCF)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company operates an integrated manufacturing facility in Punjab with capabilities across sweaters, jackets, T-shirts and other knitted products; the report says only that earlier Company disclosures had indicated significant installed capacities across these categories, and does not restate them. No new plant, line or capacity-addition project with a commissioning or ramp timeline is disclosed in this bundle. Expansion is instead framed around product diversification into knitted accessories, toys and athleisure, and around funding: during FY26 the Company initiated a preferential issue of up to 20 lakh convertible warrants at ₹115 per warrant, aggregating up to ₹23 crore, intended to support future expansion plans, strengthen working capital and enhance operational capabilities - described as aligned with a broader strategy of creating additional capacity for growth while maintaining financial flexibility, with implementation dependent on market conditions, execution capability and efficient deployment of capital. Directors state no dividend is recommended in view of continuous expansion activities. On the energy side the Company has installed a solar power system of approximately 503.04 kWp DC / 500 kW AC; this is captive generation, not manufacturing capacity. Management also lists expansion of the retail and distribution platform and entry into organised multi-brand retail (the NUEMO platform) as opportunities it intends to pursue, while acknowledging these carry execution, capital-allocation and market-acceptance risk - these remain stated intentions, not commissioned projects.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and strategic — framing US trade disruption as temporary, emphasizing automation as non-negotiable future, highlighting supplier financing as a strength, projecting Rs.700Cr revenue target with clear roadmap; tone is optimistic but grounded in operational discipline

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated design-to-manufacturing capability, described as an important competitive advantage, letting the Company support customers seeking flexibility, product differentiation and shorter development cycles
- Ability to engage brands across the full chain from product conception and development through manufacturing, distribution and retail
- Long-standing relationships with established domestic and international brands
- Manufacturing flexibility and design capabilities positioned as a platform for continued product development
- Captive renewable generation: an installed solar system of approximately 503.04 kWp DC / 500 kW AC reducing dependence on conventional electricity

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: US tariff uncertainty impacting demand visibility; Slow adoption in new European markets; Competitive pressure from displaced Chinese/other Indian suppliers; Execution risk in 3-year machine rollout; Labor cost inflation if wage hikes persist beyond 2026

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The Rs.60Cr capex is not a cash outflow — it’s supplier-financed machinery; the real capital risk is borne by Ningbo, not Active Clothing; this is a rare case of capex being funded by equipment vendor — a structural advantage

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Maintain and deepen relationships with established domestic and international apparel brands while developing additional channels to diversify the revenue base
- Continue product diversification beyond core knitwear to reduce dependence on individual product categories
- Raise growth capital through a preferential issue of convertible warrants to fund future expansion, working capital and operational capabilities
- Reinvest earnings rather than distribute them: no dividend recommended for FY2025-26 in view of continuous expansion activities, with profit transferred to reserves

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| American market disruption due to tariffs | Other Indian apparel manufacturers | loser | High | Active is less exposed than peers (only 25% export to US), and is using the disruption to build automation moat — competitors without capex will lose market share |
| Rising labor costs and retention pressure | Active Clothing Co Limited | winner | Medium | Labor cost inflation is temporary and being offset by automation — company is investing in retention to secure skilled workforce for future smart factory |
